notes: Three back-to-back no-op turns ('Reply with exactly the word: ok') in ONE interactive GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 session, then a clean /exit. SESSION MODEL: single-birth. Copilot mints ~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl at launch and the session id is that DIRECTORY (agent.go SessionIDFromPath), stable for the session's whole life — no presession reconcile, unlike codex/gemini-cli — so session_birth anchors to recording start UNPINNED, so a transient proc-<PID> presession row can't steal the birth. The state arc is unremarkable and READ rather than inferred: Copilot's turn boundaries are explicit (user.message → working, assistant.turn_end → turn_done → ready), so the phases below are three clean ready→working→ready cycles on one session id. The token-accounting evidence the scenario exists for lives in the recording's metric vector, not the phase DSL (which has no metric form). TWO token paths compose against one shared per-model high-water mark (Parser.lastUsage): (a) LIVE — every assistant.message carries data.outputTokens, queued as a PerTurnContribution{Output} increment, which is the ONLY token signal a running session has; (b) CUMULATIVE — session.shutdown carries modelMetrics.<model>.usage {inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheReadTokens,cacheWriteTokens}, queued as a DELTA against that mark, so the output half already contributed live is not re-counted and only the previously-unseen INPUT tokens land. The load-bearing verified finding: session.usage_checkpoint carries ONLY {modelCacheState,totalNanoAiu,totalPremiumRequests} — no token counts at all; modelMetrics/tokenDetails/currentTokens exist ONLY at shutdown. Contributions are non-negative deltas folded by MergeMetrics, so TotalTokens is non-decreasing: >0 after T1 (output path), ≥ prior after T2 and T3. The /exit step is load-bearing, not cosmetic — input tokens have no live signal, so without a clean session.shutdown the recording would carry output tokens only. OBSERVATIONS: tokens_nonzero + cost_nonzero are asserted; cost comes from the shared capacity price map per the #1256 decision (general token pricing, NOT reconstructed from Copilot's totalNanoAiu AI credits), and a $0 cost means a missing alias in core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go — that was the claude-haiku-4.5 (family-first, dotted) bug, now fixed. model is deliberately NOT pinned: this account offers only gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5, --model accepts only 'auto', and the router's choice can even change mid-session — record fills it from the recording. NOT ASSERTED: the scenario's third criterion (CacheReadTokens>0 with fresh input=0 on a fully-cached turn) is unattributable per turn for Copilot — cacheReadTokens exists only inside the cumulative shutdown block, so cache reads arrive as one session-total delta at exit, never bound to a turn; do NOT assert a non-zero cache bucket (same shape as the codex sibling's caveat). No teardown/process_exited phase is asserted: PID binding is CWD-based and best-effort, and the scenario's assertion is the token arc, not the exit.

Turn 1 completes back to ready on assistant.turn_end; that turn's assistant.message outputTokens is contributed live, so TotalTokens > 0 after T1 even though no shutdown line exists yet
Turn 2 user prompt → working on the same session
Turn 2 completes back to ready; TotalTokens after T2 ≥ TotalTokens after T1 (monotonic)
Turn 3 user prompt → working on the same session

Turn 3 completes back to ready; TotalTokens after T3 ≥ TotalTokens after T2 (monotonic across three turns); the session never enters waiting — these are no-op prompts with no tool calls, so no permission.requested is ever written
